assessment.summary: BRAF (P15056) is one of the most extensively validated oncology drug targets in human medicine, with 5 approved small-molecule inhibitors, over 11,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 138 PDB structures including many at high resolution with bound ligands. The target is highly druggable across multiple cancer indications driven by activating mutations (notably V600E), with a rich chemical and structural landscape supporting further drug discovery efforts.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 66.4 (55% high-confidence fraction) suggests disordered regions outside the kinase domain, but this does not limit druggability given the wealth of experimental structures
Resistance mechanisms (e.g., paradoxical MAPK activation, splice variants, BRAF amplification) remain an active challenge not fully addressed by current approved drugs
Coverage of non-V600 BRAF mutants (class II and III) in structural and chemical datasets may be less comprehensive than V600E
Allosteric and dimer-interface inhibitor strategies are still emerging and less well-characterised chemically compared to ATP-competitive inhibitors
Combination therapy optimal partners and sequencing strategies are not fully resolved in all tumour types
